children: The Russian Central Bank's forecast for a high-risk scenario sees the price of oil falling to an average of $35 per barrel next year, with gross domestic product shrinking by 3-4% and inflation rising to 11-13%, according to a document published on Monday.
In the baseline scenario, the Central Bank expects the widespread fuel shortages which have plagued Russia this summer to abate, causing only a limited impact on inflation, the document said.
